newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian masterpieces to come home - minister.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian masterpieces to come home - minister.

text.p: Indonesia has secured the return of five paintings stolen from Jakarta's National Museum which were up for sale at a Christies auction next month in Singapore, the Jakarta Post newspaper said on Friday.
"Thank God we've finally got the paintings," Education and Culture Minister Wardiman Djojonegoro said.
The paintings were taken to the Indonesian Embassy in Singapore after negotiations with an unidentified collector, the head of the National Museum, Suwati Kartiwa, was quoted as saying.

The theft was revealed after Christies published a catalogue for its October 6 sale containing five Indonesian paintings including "A Nude", completed in 1992, by Basoeki Abdullah and "Portrait of a Dutch Governor Wearing the Willems Order", painted in 1867 by Raden Saleh.
The auctioneers withdrew the two paintings last week after being informed they were stolen and withdrew the other three on Thursday.
According to the daily, the theft was reported to police on September 12 but it was only leaked to the press late last week.
Wardiman said the theft might have been motivated by the low wages of museum employees. Middle-ranking Indonesian civil servants earn only between 250,000 rupiah ($108) and 500,000 ($216) a month.
